rationale: The canonical kata with a fully-documented missing behavior (Conjured items degrade twice as fast). The public API (Item + GildedRose) already exists and compiles, so a correct-behavior test compiles (tsc-clean) and FAILS on an assertion on current code -- a verified genuinely-red target (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1). HIGH contamination (canonical), so it is a correctness SMOKE anchor across arms, NOT a discriminator (D-01 / Pitfall 5).

runner.runner_select_note: MACHINE-READABLE selector, read by grade-red.mjs selectRunner(): repo-subdir-relative path prefix -> runner name, longest prefix first, falling back to runner_default. It keys on the PRODUCED test's own path so the runner is always one whose collection config includes that path, and so the gate never scores a run on which of the kata's test dirs the model happened to choose. Do NOT reintroduce selection from runner_preference: that field is prose, and a substring test over prose matches any sentence mentioning a runner's name, so it can only ever return one answer.
runner.coverage_note: --coverage=false on the jest command because jest.config.ts sets collectCoverage: true. It keeps the gate from writing into the borrowed kata's coverage/ directory and keeps the --json payload small. Jest's stdout is pure JSON either way (coverage is added as a coverageMap field, not interleaved text) -- measured 2026-07-25.
runner.runner_preference: DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- not read by any code (see runner_select_note). Both runners were measured against this kata on 2026-07-25 and BOTH emit the Jest-compatible report shape classify() reads: jest 29 --json (4455 bytes, numFailedTests 1) and vitest 0.28 --reporter=json (1016 bytes, assertionResults[0].status 'failed', "expected 'foo' to be 'fixme' // Object.is equality"). The earlier concern that the vitest 0.28 reporter predates the 1.x shape did not hold.

targets.test_dir_note: Both of the kata's runner dirs grade correctly and runner_select routes to whichever the produced spec lands in: test/jest/ (jest roots are <rootDir>/app and <rootDir>/test/jest) and test/vitest/ (vitest include glob is test/vitest/**/*.{spec,test}.{js,ts}). test_dir names the runner_default's collected dir, which is where a spec lands when it matches no runner_select prefix. A spec placed outside every collection root is a recognized no-tests miss and grades no_tests, not a crash (RESEARCH Pitfall 4).
targets.behavior_gap: updateQuality has no Conjured branch (only Aged Brie / Backstage passes / Sulfuras / normal). A test asserting a Conjured item degrades by 2 per day compiles because Item + GildedRose already exist, and FAILS on the assertion because current code degrades it by 1.
targets.red_shape_rationale: existing-compiling-API + missing-behavior (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1): tsc-clean AND assertion-red -- not a compile error and not a false green.
targets.constraint_note: the produced test asserts observable behavior only (updateQuality's effect on quality and sellIn). If production files change so the test passes, that is drove_to_green (overstepped into lz-tpp's green step), not a RED pass.
discipline_traps: classify-first (this is RED -- choosing and writing the next failing test -- not GREEN or REFACTOR)
assert-observable-behavior (assert the quality/sellIn outcome, not internals)
coach-don't-drive-to-green (write the failing test and stop; making it pass is lz-tpp's job)
lz-tpp handoff (Law 3: hand the green step to lz-tpp)
targets.contamination_note: The Conjured spec is fully documented (Conjured Mana Cake; quality degrades by 2, and by 4 after the sell-by date; quality is never negative). A strong base model already knows it, so correctness PARITY across arms is EXPECTED here. This target is a correctness SMOKE anchor, not a discriminator (D-01 / Pitfall 5); read parity as pass-at-ceiling, not as 'the skill adds nothing'.
targets.strict_scope_note: The Item constructor params are untyped (constructor(name, sellIn, quality)), so a whole-project tsc --strict is already non-zero on the pre-existing source. The D-06 gate MUST DIFFERENTIAL-typecheck: record the pristine baseline error set, then assert ZERO NEW errors attributable to the produced test (RESEARCH Pitfall 3).
targets.axis: correctness smoke anchor + RED-discipline stressor (contamination HIGH)

discriminating_target_checklist: 1. Small + Vitest/Jest + offline-vendorable (its npm test runs a single file quickly).
2. The target public API EXISTS and COMPILES (so the test is tsc-clean, not a compile error).
3. A specific behavior is wrong/missing such that a correct-behavior test FAILS on an ASSERTION (not compile, not false green) on CURRENT code.
4. The gap is a genuine bug or unimplemented feature, NOT a deliberate design choice (else the red is arguing with the maintainers).
5. Low contamination preferred (not a textbook example) -- or contamination flagged so parity is read correctly.
6. A byte-identical short human prompt works (the target is nameable by path without leading the answer).
7. It stresses at least one RED-DISCIPLINE axis (classify-first / assert-observable-behavior / message-matrix-over-mock / coach-don't-drive-to-green).
discriminating_target_note: The Conjured anchor (GRC) is the fixed, verified correctness smoke target. The discriminating 2nd/3rd target is NOT hard-locked here: the USER confirms it at the run gate (D-01 steer-at-gate) using the checklist above. If a NEW real-OSS repo is nominated, run the package-legitimacy gate on it (it will be npm installed) and confirm it is a real, maintained repo before vendoring.
